title: What Is PasteGuard? Features, Status and Risks (2026)
summary: What is PasteGuard? This tool screens text before sending to AI systems, helping you understand what safeguards it provides and whether to use it.
body_markdown:
## Connecting PasteGuard to an Activepieces workflow today


### What the pilot needs from the docs


Because Activepieces ships nothing specific to PasteGuard, the pilot you just specified must be assembled from general building blocks, which cost nothing extra in flow count since every plan allows unlimited flows, and we haven't run any of them.


Each of three routes depends on one fact that PasteGuard's documentation has to state.


For an HTTP request step, you need the documented endpoint, request body and response format.


An AI step with an OpenAI-compatible provider needs the docs to say PasteGuard accepts that API format at a base URL you can set. An MCP server needs the docs to describe an MCP interface at all.


### What it costs to run


Metering follows the plan. The[Activepieces pricing page](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) lists 1000 credits a month on Free ($0), 10000 on Plus ($20) and 50000 on Team ($200).


Free therefore suits only a handful of test pastes, so run one workflow and read its credit cost before you choose a plan.


### Three ways to connect PasteGuard compared


Simplest of the three is the HTTP request step: one step sends the text to PasteGuard and the next step reads the reply. Everything rests on the documented request and response shapes. If the docs don't show them, stop here.


With the AI step, PasteGuard sits between the workflow and the model. It works only if the docs confirm the compatible format and the base URL. Test with the cable pulled to see whether anything leaves the machine.


Most complex is the MCP server, because the model decides when to call the tool. A model that skips the call skips the checkpoint, so treat this as the last option to trust.


Activepieces, which MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run, lets you avoid that dependence: in its flow builder an HTTP request step can sit ahead of an Agent step in the same flow, so the check is a fixed step the model never gets to skip, and the run trace shows the PasteGuard call and the Agent step listed in order inside one execution record, rather than in two systems bridged by a callback.


Whichever you build, the log it leaves is what the next section examines.
